name: Fast Company

sources.title: Fast Company contributor guidelines — Work Life section accepts complete unpublished drafts; 'no pitches, abstracts, outlines, press releases, or interview offers'
Fast Company Help Center — Impact Council members can submit thought-leadership pieces working with an editor (paid membership route)
Fast Company Editorial Guidelines and AI Use Policy (identified via search result)

conditions: Free path exists but is selective: the Work Life section accepts contributed articles as complete drafts only — editors choose what to publish
A paid membership route (Impact Council) lets members work with an editor to submit thought-leadership pieces
requirements: Contributed pieces go to the Work Life section (productivity, creativity, career development, hiring, work culture, entrepreneurship, DEI, innovation)
Send a complete unpublished draft — pitches, abstracts, outlines, press releases, and interview offers are explicitly rejected
Written by a person, not a PR department; over-the-top self-promotion kills the piece
Secondary coverage reports submissions go to submissions@fastcompany.com, ~700–1,000 words, with ~5 business days as the move-on window and 24h exclusivity after publication
Contributors are unpaid but retain copyright (per editor guidance found in search results)
preparation: A finished, polished ~700–1,000-word op-ed-style article — not a product announcement
A leadership/workplace/innovation thesis with original ideas; anecdotes plus research
Author bio establishing credibility in the industry covered
If pursuing paid recognition instead: Most Innovative Companies applications (micapplications@fastcompany.com) or Impact Council membership
workflow: Read the contributor guidelines article on fastcompany.com
Write a complete draft matching the Work Life voice — op-ed, not content marketing
Submit the full draft to the submissions inbox (submissions@fastcompany.com per secondary sources) or the current Work Life editor
Wait roughly five business days; no reply means move on — they ask you not to follow up
If published, keep it exclusive to Fast Company for 24 hours, then repost with a link to the original
watchFor: Do not send a pitch or outline — only complete drafts are considered
Self-promotional content about your own company/product is a stated disqualifier — a SaaS launch does not fit this format
Multiple editor emails exist (section editors change); verify the current Work Life editor before sending
Impact Council and awards (MIC) are paid/application routes — different products, do not confuse with earned coverage
countsAsLive: A contributed article is published under the Work Life section at fastcompany.com/section/contributed-content
unknowns: Current Work Life section editor and whether the submissions@fastcompany.com inbox is still the intake
